title:	Choose PDF library and download a basic budget PDF
state:	CLOSED
author:	jamesleonard3rd (James Leonard)
labels:	scope: medium
comments:	2
assignees:	TigerK9 (Liam McLemore)
projects:	
milestone:	Sprint 1
number:	60

## Summary
Sub-issue of #57. This is the first of three sub-issues for PDF export of a budget month, and depends on the CSV sub-issue (#<CSV issue number>).

Before we can draw a PDF, we need two things: an approved PDF library, and the budget data turned into the exact rows the PDF will show. This issue does both. The library comparison and the row-building code don't depend on each other, so two people can work on them at the same time. Nothing visible to users ships in this issue; it sets up the rendering sub-issues that follow.

## User Story
As a user who wants to share my budget as a PDF, I want the PDF to be built on a reliable library and to show exactly the same numbers as my budget page, so that the document I hand to others is accurate and readable.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. At least three PDF libraries (for example jsPDF with jspdf-autotable, pdfmake, and @react-pdf/renderer) are compared on bundle size, table and page-break support, repeating headers, license, and fit with our React/TypeScript codebase.
2. Each library is tested on whether its built-in fonts display common currency symbols (such as €, £, ¥, ₹) and non-English category names, and the write-up says whether we will need to embed a font and roughly how much that would add to the download.
3. The comparison and a recommendation are posted as a comment on this issue, and the team approves one library before sub-issue B starts.
4. The team decides whether the PDF supports envelope budgets, tracking budgets, or both (matching the CSV sub-issue), and whether "To Budget" / overbudgeted appears at the top in envelope mode. The decisions are recorded on this issue.
5. A function takes the month data collected by the CSV sub-issue and returns an ordered list of PDF rows. Each row is marked as a group header, category, group subtotal, or grand total.
6. Rows include every visible category group and category in the same order as the budget page, with **Budgeted**, **Spent**, and **Balance** values.
7. Values match the budget page for that month, including carryover balances.
8. Amounts are already formatted as text using the user's configured currency and number format, the same way they appear in the app.
9. The row-building function does not depend on the chosen PDF library, so it can be written before the library decision.
10. There are unit tests for row order, group subtotals, grand totals, carryover, and amount formatting, including a group with no visible categories and a negative balance.

## Out of Scope
- Anything already covered by the CSV sub-issue (month selection, data collection, the Export action itself).
- Adding the library to the project, or any PDF rendering or download (sub-issue B).
- Page breaks, repeated headers, page numbers, row styling, and cross-browser checks (sub-issue C).
- Embedding a font; this issue only decides whether one is needed.
- The mobile budget page.

## Open Questions
1. **Shared code with CSV:** Can the row-building function reuse part of the CSV export's code, or should the CSV export use these rows too so the two formats can't drift apart?
2. **Hidden categories:** Should hidden categories and groups be left out of the PDF the same way they are hidden on the budget page, or follow a separate setting?
3. **Decision owner:** Who gives final approval on the library choice?

## Rough Scope
Medium. The library comparison is research, but it needs small hands-on tests of each option (a sample multi-page table, currency symbols, bundle size), not only reading their docs. The row-building function is a focused piece of logic, but getting carryover, subtotals, ordering, and formatting to match the budget page exactly needs careful testing. Neither part touches the UI.

## Source
Split from #57, which was too large for one issue. This is sub-issue A of 3: (A) library choice and table rows, (B) PDF export option and one-page PDF, (C) multi-page layout and cross-platform checks.

---ISSUE61---
title:	PDF export: add PDF option to Export menu, polish layout, and verify across platforms (dependent on #60)
state:	OPEN
author:	jamesleonard3rd (James Leonard)
labels:	scope: medium
comments:	0
assignees:	TigerK9 (Liam McLemore)
projects:	
milestone:	Sprint 1
number:	61
--
## Summary
Sub-issue of #57. This is the second of two sub-issues for PDF export of a budget month, and depends on #60 (PR #75), which picked the PDF library (jsPDF + jspdf-autotable) and added `buildBudgetMonthPdfRows`.

#60 shipped nothing users can see. This issue adds the **PDF** option to the budget page's existing **Export** button (added by the CSV export in #56 / PR #71). It also makes the downloaded PDF readable and reliable for real budgets: it handles budgets that run past one page, makes the table easy to scan, shows all characters correctly, and looks the same everywhere users can export it.

Most of the plumbing already exists from the CSV export and #60, so this issue should reuse it rather than rebuild it:

| Already exists | Where | Reused for |
|---|---|---|
| Export button and month menu, with an `exporters` map keyed by format | `components/budget/BudgetExportMenu.tsx` | Add a `pdf` entry next to `csv` |
| Visible-month calculation | `getVisibleMonths` in `components/budget/MonthsContext.tsx` | Same month choices as CSV |
| Fetching a month's budget cells | `fetchBudgetMonthCells` in `export/budgetMonthCsv.ts` | Same data source as CSV |
| Row traversal shared by CSV and PDF | `collectBudgetMonthRows` in `export/budgetMonthRows.ts` (PR #75) | Same rows and numbers as CSV |
| Typed, pre-formatted PDF rows | `buildBudgetMonthPdfRows` in `export/budgetMonthPdfRows.ts` (PR #75) | Table body for jspdf-autotable |
| Filename cleanup | `getBudgetMonthCsvFilename` in `export/budgetMonthCsv.ts` | Generalize to take an extension (`.csv` / `.pdf`) |
| Saving a file (browser download, or the Electron save dialog) | `window.Actual.saveFile` | Already accepts binary data (used for the `.zip` budget export) |
| Error notification when an export fails | `onMenuSelect` in `BudgetExportMenu.tsx` | Unchanged |

## User Story
As a user sharing my budget with a financial advisor or partner, I want to export the selected budget month as a clean, professional PDF from the same Export button I use for CSV, no matter how large my budget is or where I export it from, so that it's easy for others to read.

## Acceptance Criteria
**Export option and download**
1. The budget page's **Export** button offers **PDF** next to **CSV**. With one month displayed, the menu shows "Export as CSV" and "Export as PDF". With several months displayed, it shows a CSV section and a PDF section, each listing the visible months (from `getVisibleMonths`).
2. PDF is added as a new `pdf` entry in `BudgetExportMenu`'s `ExportFormat` / `exporters` map. The CSV path does not change.
3. Choosing PDF downloads a `.pdf` file named `<budget-name>-<YYYY-MM>.pdf`, with no print dialog. The filename helper is shared with CSV, so both formats clean up the name the same way.
4. The PDF is saved through `window.Actual.saveFile`, the same call the CSV export uses. That means a direct download in the browser and the platform save dialog in Electron. This answers #57 Open Question 5.
5. The PDF data comes from `fetchBudgetMonthCells` and `buildBudgetMonthPdfRows`, with amounts formatted by the user's `useFormat()` currency settings. The PDF exporter does not walk categories or read spreadsheet cells itself, so its numbers always match the CSV and the budget page.
6. jsPDF and jspdf-autotable are added as dependencies and loaded with a dynamic `import()` only when the user picks PDF. They must not appear in the main bundle.
7. Like CSV, the Export button stays limited to envelope budgets. If a PDF fails to generate, the existing "Failed to export the budget month." notification is shown.

**Layout and polish**

8. The PDF has a title with the budget name and month, plus Budgeted / Spent / Balance columns. It contains no app navigation, sidebars, or buttons.
9. Budgets that run past one page break cleanly between rows, with column headers repeated on each page and page numbers.
10. Group header rows and total rows (`groupHeader` / `grandTotal` from `PdfRow.type`) are visually distinct from category rows, for example bold text or shading.
11. Long category names wrap or shorten without overlapping other columns.
12. Currency symbols and non-English category names display correctly. #60 found that the built-in fonts cover €, £ and ¥ but not ₹ or non-Latin text. If we embed a font (for example Noto Sans), it is loaded lazily with the library, and its added download size is noted in the PR.
13. The PDF looks the same when exported from Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and the desktop (Electron) app.

**Tests**

14. Unit tests cover the PDF menu entries (single month and multiple months), the shared filename helper for both extensions, and the mapping from `PdfRow`s to the autotable body and styles. The existing CSV tests still pass unchanged.

## Out of Scope
- Changes to the row data or the library choice (done in #60).
- Changes to the CSV output.
- Tracking budgets (the Export button is envelope-only, same as CSV).
- Customizing the PDF's layout, colors, columns, or branding.
- Exporting more than one month, charts, or notes.
- The mobile budget page.

## Open Questions
1. **Fonts:** Do we embed a Unicode font now to cover ₹ and non-Latin names, or ship with the built-in fonts and track embedding as a follow-up?
2. **Long names:** Should long category names wrap onto multiple lines or be shortened with an ellipsis?
3. **Menu layout:** With several months displayed, should the menu be grouped by format (CSV section, then PDF section) or by month (each month with CSV/PDF options)?
4. **To Budget row:** #60 placed "To Budget" / "Overbudgeted" after the grand total and tagged it `grandTotal`. Should the PDF style it differently from the Total row?

## Rough Scope
Medium–large. This used to be only layout polish; it now also includes adding the dependency, lazy-loading it, the menu entry, and saving the file. Reusing the CSV export's menu, data fetch, filename and save logic, plus #60's row builder, keeps the new code mostly limited to the jsPDF rendering function. Page breaks, repeated headers and page numbers are built into jspdf-autotable. Font embedding (Open Question 1) and testing in three browsers and Electron are where most of the extra time will go.

## Source
Split from #57. Sub-issue 2 of 2; builds on #60 (PR #75) and reuses the CSV export from #56 (PR #71). This merges the earlier planned sub-issue B ("PDF export option and one-page PDF") into this issue, so #57 is now covered by two sub-issues instead of three.

import { useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { Trans, useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';

import { Button } from '@actual-app/components/button';
import { SvgDownloadThickBottom } from '@actual-app/components/icons/v2';
import { Menu } from '@actual-app/components/menu';
import { Popover } from '@actual-app/components/popover';
import { send } from '@actual-app/core/platform/client/connection';
import * as monthUtils from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';

import { useCategories } from '#hooks/useCategories';
import { useFormat } from '#hooks/useFormat';
import { useGlobalPref } from '#hooks/useGlobalPref';
import { useLocale } from '#hooks/useLocale';
import { useLocalPref } from '#hooks/useLocalPref';
import { useMetadataPref } from '#hooks/useMetadataPref';
import { addNotification } from '#notifications/notificationsSlice';
import { useDispatch } from '#redux';

import { useBudgetMonthCount } from './BudgetMonthCountContext';
import {
  buildBudgetMonthCsv,
  fetchBudgetMonthCells,
  getBudgetMonthCsvFilename,
} from './export/budgetMonthCsv';
import { getVisibleMonths } from './MonthsContext';
import type { MonthBounds } from './MonthsContext';

type ExportFormat = 'csv';

type ExportAction = {
  format: ExportFormat;
  month: string;
};

export function BudgetExportMenu() {
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const dispatch = useDispatch();
  const locale = useLocale();
  const format = useFormat();
  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
  const [monthBounds, setMonthBounds] = useState<MonthBounds | null>(null);

  const [startMonthPref] = useLocalPref('budget.startMonth');
  const [maxMonthsPref] = useGlobalPref('maxMonths');
  const [showHiddenCategories = false] = useLocalPref(
    'budget.showHiddenCategories',
  );
  const [budgetName] = useMetadataPref('budgetName');
  const { displayMax } = useBudgetMonthCount();
  const { data: { grouped: categoryGroups } = { grouped: [] } } =
    useCategories();

  // Mirrors how the budget page picks the months it displays.
  const startMonth = startMonthPref || monthUtils.currentMonth();
  const numMonths = Math.min(displayMax, maxMonthsPref || 1);
  const months = monthBounds
    ? getVisibleMonths(startMonth, numMonths, monthBounds)
    : [];

  const actions = new Map<string, ExportAction>(
    months.map(month => [`csv:${month}`, { format: 'csv', month }]),
  );

  const exporters: Record<ExportFormat, (month: string) => Promise<void>> = {
    csv: async month => {
      const cells = await fetchBudgetMonthCells(month);
      const csv = buildBudgetMonthCsv({
        month,
        categoryGroups,
        cells,
        showHiddenCategories,
        decimalPlaces: format.currency.decimalPlaces,
      });
      await window.Actual.saveFile(
        csv,
        getBudgetMonthCsvFilename(budgetName, month),
        t('Export budget month'),
      );
    },
  };

  async function onOpen() {
    setMonthBounds(await send('get-budget-bounds'));
    setIsOpen(true);
  }

  async function onMenuSelect(name: string) {
    setIsOpen(false);

    const action = actions.get(name);
    if (!action) {
      return;
    }

    try {
      await exporters[action.format](action.month);
    } catch {
      dispatch(
        addNotification({
          notification: {
            type: 'error',
            message: t('Failed to export the budget month.'),
          },
        }),
      );
    }
  }

  const csvItems =
    months.length === 1
      ? [{ name: `csv:${months[0]}`, text: t('Export as CSV') }]
      : [
          { type: Menu.label, name: t('CSV'), text: '' } as const,
          ...months.map(month => ({
            name: `csv:${month}`,
            text: monthUtils.format(month, 'MMMM yyyy', locale),
          })),
        ];

  return (
    <>
      <Button
        ref={triggerRef}
        variant="bare"
        aria-label={t('Export budget month')}
        onPress={() => void onOpen()}
        style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 4 }}
      >
        <SvgDownloadThickBottom width={13} height={13} />
        <Trans>Export</Trans>
      </Button>

      <Popover
        placement="bottom start"
        triggerRef={triggerRef}
        isOpen={isOpen}
        onOpenChange={() => setIsOpen(false)}
      >
        <Menu onMenuSelect={name => void onMenuSelect(name)} items={csvItems} />
      </Popover>
    </>
  );
}

import { send } from '@actual-app/core/platform/client/connection';
import { integerToAmount } from '@actual-app/core/shared/util';
import type { CategoryGroupEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
import { t } from 'i18next';

import { stringifyCsv } from '#util/csv';

import { collectBudgetMonthRows } from './budgetMonthRows';

type BudgetMonthCells = Map<string, unknown>;

type BuildBudgetMonthCsvOptions = {
  month: string;
  categoryGroups: CategoryGroupEntity[];
  cells: BudgetMonthCells;
  showHiddenCategories: boolean;
  decimalPlaces: number;
};

type CsvRow = [string, string, number | '', number | '', number | ''];

// Builds a CSV of one envelope budget month, mirroring the rows and values
// shown on the budget page. Subtotals and totals come from the spreadsheet's
// own group/total cells so they always match what the page displays.
export function buildBudgetMonthCsv({
  month,
  categoryGroups,
  cells,
  showHiddenCategories,
  decimalPlaces,
}: BuildBudgetMonthCsvOptions): string {
  function amount(value: number | null): number | '' {
    return value == null ? '' : integerToAmount(value, decimalPlaces);
  }

  const rawRows = collectBudgetMonthRows({
    month,
    categoryGroups,
    cells,
    showHiddenCategories,
  });

  const rows: CsvRow[] = rawRows.map(row => [
    row.groupName,
    row.categoryName,
    amount(row.budgeted),
    amount(row.spent),
    amount(row.balance),
  ]);

  return stringifyCsv(rows, [
    t('Category Group'),
    t('Category'),
    t('Budgeted'),
    t('Spent'),
    t('Balance'),
  ]);
}

export function getBudgetMonthCsvFilename(
  budgetName: string | undefined,
  month: string,
): string {
  const safeName = (budgetName ?? '').replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, '').trim();
  return `${safeName || 'budget'}-${month}.csv`;
}

export async function fetchBudgetMonthCells(
  month: string,
): Promise<BudgetMonthCells> {
  const values = await send('envelope-budget-month', { month });
  return new Map(values.map(({ name, value }) => [name, value]));
}

import type { CategoryGroupEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';

import { collectBudgetMonthRows } from './budgetMonthRows';
import type { RawBudgetMonthRowKind } from './budgetMonthRows';

// The envelope budget page renders a category group's name and its
// Budgeted/Spent/Balance as one combined, bold row (see
// `CategoryGroupMonth` in EnvelopeBudgetComponents.tsx) — there is no
// separate header-then-subtotal split to preserve. `groupHeader` is used for
// that combined row; `groupSubtotal` is kept in the type for the renderer's
// vocabulary (per the issue's acceptance criteria) but is never emitted here.
export type PdfRowType =
  | 'groupHeader'
  | 'category'
  | 'groupSubtotal'
  | 'grandTotal';

export type PdfRow = {
  type: PdfRowType;
  categoryGroup: string;
  category: string;
  // Already formatted for display; '' for a blank cell.
  budgeted: string;
  spent: string;
  balance: string;
};

const ROW_TYPE_BY_KIND: Record<RawBudgetMonthRowKind, PdfRowType> = {
  group: 'groupHeader',
  category: 'category',
  income: 'groupHeader',
  incomeCategory: 'category',
  total: 'grandTotal',
  toBudget: 'grandTotal',
};

type BuildBudgetMonthPdfRowsOptions = {
  month: string;
  categoryGroups: CategoryGroupEntity[];
  cells: Map<string, unknown>;
  showHiddenCategories: boolean;
  // Formats a raw integer-cent amount using the user's configured currency
  // and number format, e.g. a `useFormat()`-bound closure for the
  // 'financial' type.
  formatAmount: (value: number) => string;
};

// Turns one envelope budget month into an ordered list of PDF table rows,
// reusing the same row traversal the CSV export uses so the two formats
// show identical numbers. Each row is tagged with the kind of row it is so
// a renderer can style group/total rows distinctly from category rows.
export function buildBudgetMonthPdfRows({
  month,
  categoryGroups,
  cells,
  showHiddenCategories,
  formatAmount,
}: BuildBudgetMonthPdfRowsOptions): PdfRow[] {
  function amount(value: number | null): string {
    return value == null ? '' : formatAmount(value);
  }

  return collectBudgetMonthRows({
    month,
    categoryGroups,
    cells,
    showHiddenCategories,
  }).map(row => ({
    type: ROW_TYPE_BY_KIND[row.kind],
    categoryGroup: row.groupName,
    category: row.categoryName,
    budgeted: amount(row.budgeted),
    spent: amount(row.spent),
    balance: amount(row.balance),
  }));
}

import * as monthUtils from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';
import type { CategoryGroupEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
import { t } from 'i18next';

import { separateGroups } from '#components/budget/util';
import { envelopeBudget } from '#spreadsheet/bindings';

export type RawBudgetMonthRowKind =
  | 'group'
  | 'category'
  | 'income'
  | 'incomeCategory'
  | 'total'
  | 'toBudget';

export type RawBudgetMonthRow = {
  kind: RawBudgetMonthRowKind;
  groupName: string;
  // '' for group/total/toBudget rows.
  categoryName: string;
  // Raw integer cents read from the sheet cell, not yet scaled by the
  // currency's decimal places. `null` means the page shows a blank cell.
  budgeted: number | null;
  spent: number | null;
  balance: number | null;
};

type CollectBudgetMonthRowsOptions = {
  month: string;
  categoryGroups: CategoryGroupEntity[];
  cells: Map<string, unknown>;
  showHiddenCategories: boolean;
};

// Walks one envelope budget month's category groups/categories in page
// order and reads their Budgeted/Spent/Balance values from the same
// spreadsheet cells the page displays, so every consumer (CSV, PDF, ...)
// shows identical numbers and can never drift apart.
export function collectBudgetMonthRows({
  month,
  categoryGroups,
  cells,
  showHiddenCategories,
}: CollectBudgetMonthRowsOptions): RawBudgetMonthRow[] {
  const sheetName = monthUtils.sheetForMonth(month);

  function cellValue(name: string) {
    const value = cells.get(`${sheetName}!${name}`);
    return typeof value === 'number' ? value : 0;
  }

  function isVisible(item: { hidden?: boolean }) {
    return showHiddenCategories || !item.hidden;
  }

  const [expenseGroups, incomeGroup] = separateGroups(categoryGroups);
  const rows: RawBudgetMonthRow[] = [];

  for (const group of expenseGroups.filter(isVisible)) {
    rows.push({
      kind: 'group',
      groupName: group.name,
      categoryName: '',
      budgeted: cellValue(envelopeBudget.groupBudgeted(group.id)),
      spent: cellValue(envelopeBudget.groupSumAmount(group.id)),
      balance: cellValue(envelopeBudget.groupBalance(group.id)),
    });

    for (const category of (group.categories ?? []).filter(isVisible)) {
      rows.push({
        kind: 'category',
        groupName: group.name,
        categoryName: category.name,
        budgeted: cellValue(envelopeBudget.catBudgeted(category.id)),
        spent: cellValue(envelopeBudget.catSumAmount(category.id)),
        balance: cellValue(envelopeBudget.catBalance(category.id)),
      });
    }
  }

  // The income group is always shown on the page, even when marked hidden.
  if (incomeGroup) {
    rows.push({
      kind: 'income',
      groupName: incomeGroup.name,
      categoryName: '',
      budgeted: null,
      spent: cellValue(envelopeBudget.groupIncomeReceived),
      balance: null,
    });

    for (const category of (incomeGroup.categories ?? []).filter(isVisible)) {
      rows.push({
        kind: 'incomeCategory',
        groupName: incomeGroup.name,
        categoryName: category.name,
        budgeted: null,
        spent: cellValue(envelopeBudget.catSumAmount(category.id)),
        balance: null,
      });
    }
  }

  // `total-budgeted` is stored negated; the page flips it back for display.
  rows.push({
    kind: 'total',
    groupName: t('Total'),
    categoryName: '',
    budgeted: -cellValue(envelopeBudget.totalBudgeted),
    spent: cellValue(envelopeBudget.totalSpent),
    balance: cellValue(envelopeBudget.totalBalance),
  });

  const toBudget = cellValue(envelopeBudget.toBudget);
  rows.push({
    kind: 'toBudget',
    groupName: toBudget < 0 ? t('Overbudgeted') : t('To Budget'),
    categoryName: '',
    budgeted: null,
    spent: null,
    balance: toBudget,
  });

  return rows;
}
```

3715:Compared bundle size (npm + bundlephobia, gzip), license, and table/page-break support for the three libraries the issue suggests:
3719:| jsPDF + jspdf-autotable | ~130KB + ~10KB ≈ **140KB** | MIT | `autoTable()` plugin, purpose-built for tabular reports | Built-in: rows never split across pages, `showHead: 'everyPage'` repeats the header row, automatic page numbering via hooks |
3723:**Fonts/currency symbols:** all three ship only the standard Latin (WinAnsi) fonts by default. That covers €, £, and ¥, but **not** ₹ or non-Latin category names (e.g. Cyrillic, CJK, Devanagari) in any of them — all three would need a custom embedded font (e.g. Noto Sans) for full Unicode support. Embedding adds roughly 150–300KB gzip depending on script coverage, and is tracked as a follow-up rather than part of this issue.
3725:**Recommendation: jsPDF + jspdf-autotable.** It's by far the smallest (~140KB vs. 342–442KB), has first-class support for exactly this report shape (tabular, non-splitting rows, repeating headers, page numbers), and is the most mature/widely used of the three. @react-pdf/renderer's JSX API would fit this codebase's declarative style more naturally, but it's the heaviest option and has no built-in table component, so we'd be rebuilding what jspdf-autotable already provides. Since the PDF library will be lazy-loaded only on export (per #57 AC#11), bundle size mainly affects export latency rather than app startup, but smaller is still better there.

# Issue #61 — PDF export menu option, layout polish, cross-platform verification

## Context

Issue #57 (PDF export of a budget month) was split into two sub-issues. #60
(PR #75, merged) picked the PDF library (jsPDF + jspdf-autotable, ~140KB
gzip) and built the data layer: `collectBudgetMonthRows` (shared row
traversal, extracted from the CSV exporter) and `buildBudgetMonthPdfRows`
(typed, pre-formatted `PdfRow[]`). It shipped **nothing visible** — no
dependency installed, no button, no rendering.

**Important finding from #60's ai-log**: #61's own issue body assumes a
separate "sub-issue B" already produced a basic one-page PDF download for
this issue to merely polish. That sub-issue B was never filed — #61 is the
only remaining issue, so it has to do both: wire up the actual PDF button
*and* the layout polish (page breaks, repeating headers, long names, fonts,
cross-platform checks). This plan treats #61 as the issue that makes PDF
export real.

Per the issue's own table, most plumbing already exists and should be reused
as-is: `BudgetExportMenu.tsx`'s exporter map, `getVisibleMonths`,
`fetchBudgetMonthCells`, `collectBudgetMonthRows`, `buildBudgetMonthPdfRows`,
`window.Actual.saveFile`, and the CSV export's error-notification path. The
only genuinely new code is the jsPDF rendering function and the menu/filename
plumbing to reach it.

**Decisions locked in during planning** (answers to #61's Open Questions):

- **Open Question 1 (fonts)**: Ship with jsPDF's built-in fonts (covers
  €/£/¥). Do **not** embed a Unicode font in this PR. Note the ₹/non-Latin
  gap explicitly in the PR description, and file a short follow-up GitHub
  issue for embedding a font (e.g. Noto Sans) later.
- **Open Question 3 (menu layout)**: Already answered by AC1 itself — group
  by format (a CSV section and a PDF section when multiple months are
  shown), mirroring the existing CSV-only menu's single/multi-month split.
- **Open Question 4 (To Budget vs Total styling)**: Same visual style for
  both — they already share `PdfRow.type: 'grandTotal'` in the data model
  from #60, so no new discriminator is needed.
- **Open Question 2 (long names)**: Use jspdf-autotable's default `wrap`
  behavior (no ellipsis) — least lossy, requires no extra code, and
  satisfies AC11 ("wrap or shorten without overlap").

## Branching

- Local `master` is 6 commits behind `origin/master` (PR #75 is merged
  there but not pulled locally). Update local `master` via fast-forward pull
  before branching — do **not** branch off the current
  `feat/issue-62-goal-card-scaffold` branch, which is unrelated (GoalCard
  widget scaffold, issue #62) and would drag its commits into this PR.
- New branch name, matching the `feat/issue-<N>-<slug>` convention used by
  `feat/issue-60-pdf-library-rows` and `feat/issue-62-goal-card-scaffold`:
  **`feat/issue-61-pdf-export-menu`**, created off the updated `master`.

## Implementation

### 1. Add dependencies

Add `jspdf` (4.2.1) and `jspdf-autotable` (5.0.8) to
`packages/desktop-client/package.json`. Both are MIT-licensed, already
vetted in #60. They are imported only via dynamic `import()` at export time
(see step 2) so they must not be referenced anywhere in static import
graphs — no top-level `import` of either package in any file that ships in
the main bundle.

### 2. New PDF rendering module

New file: `packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/export/budgetMonthPdf.ts`

- `buildBudgetMonthPdfBytes(options): Promise<Uint8Array>` (name indicative;
  final signature decided during implementation) that:
  - Dynamically imports `jspdf` and `jspdf-autotable`
    (`const { jsPDF } = await import('jspdf'); const autoTable = (await import('jspdf-autotable')).default;`).
  - Takes the already-built `PdfRow[]` from `buildBudgetMonthPdfRows`
    (reused unchanged from #60 — this module does **not** walk categories or
    read cells itself, per AC5) plus the month/budget name for the title.
  - Builds the document: title text (budget name + formatted month),
    Budgeted/Spent/Balance columns via `autoTable()`.
  - Uses autoTable's built-in `showHead: 'everyPage'` for repeating headers
    and its automatic page-number hook — both are built-in behavior per
    #60's research, not new code to write.
  - Maps each `PdfRow` to an autotable body row plus a style for
    `groupHeader` / `grandTotal` rows (bold/shaded) vs plain `category` rows,
    via a small pure helper (e.g. `toAutoTableRows(rows: PdfRow[])`) kept
    separable from the jsPDF calls so it can be unit-tested without
    constructing a real `jsPDF` instance.
  - Returns the PDF as bytes (`doc.output('arraybuffer')` wrapped for
    `window.Actual.saveFile`, which accepts `string | Buffer`).

### 3. Generalize the filename helper

In `packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/export/budgetMonthCsv.ts`,
`getBudgetMonthCsvFilename` is CSV-specific. Per the issue's own table this
helper should be shared and take an extension. Options to decide during
implementation (lean toward the simpler one):
- Move/rename to a format-agnostic helper (e.g. `getBudgetMonthExportFilename(budgetName, month, extension)`) in a shared location (`budgetMonthRows.ts` or a new small `budgetMonthFilename.ts`), with `budgetMonthCsv.ts` and the new PDF module both calling it.
- Keep it in `budgetMonthCsv.ts` but add an `extension` parameter and re-export for PDF use.

Either way: no change to the CSV filename output; add a corresponding test
for the `.pdf` extension.

### 4. Wire the menu

In `packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/BudgetExportMenu.tsx`:

- Widen `type ExportFormat = 'csv'` to `'csv' | 'pdf'`.
- Add a `pdf` entry to the `exporters` map that calls
  `fetchBudgetMonthCells` → `buildBudgetMonthPdfRows` (with `formatAmount`
  bound to `useFormat()`) → the new rendering function → `window.Actual.saveFile(bytes, filename, t('Export budget month'))`.
- Extend the `actions` map to register `pdf:${month}` actions alongside the
  existing `csv:${month}` ones.
- Extend the menu items construction: single month → `["Export as CSV", "Export as PDF"]`; multiple months → a CSV section (unchanged) followed by a PDF section, each listing the visible months — mirroring the existing `csvItems` single/multi-month branch exactly, per AC1 and the Open-Question-3 resolution above.
- No change to `onMenuSelect` / error-notification path — it already looks
  up `actions.get(name)` generically and reports the existing
  "Failed to export the budget month." notification on any thrown error,
  satisfying AC7.
- No change to the envelope-only restriction — this component is already
  only rendered for envelope budgets (CSV's existing behavior).

### 5. Tests

- `budgetMonthPdf.test.ts` (new): unit test the pure
  `PdfRow[] → autotable body/styles` mapping function (AC14) without
  constructing a real jsPDF document — mock/avoid the `jspdf`/`jspdf-autotable`
  imports in this test, consistent with #60's existing
  `budgetMonthPdfRows.test.ts` conventions (plain data in, plain data out,
  `vitest` `describe`/`it`/`expect`).
- `BudgetExportMenu.test.tsx` (new, none currently exists): test the menu
  item generation for single-month and multi-month cases, confirming both a
  CSV and PDF entry/section appear (AC1, AC14).
- `budgetMonthCsv.test.ts` / wherever the filename helper tests live: add a
  case for the `.pdf` extension share, confirm `.csv` output is unchanged
  (AC3, AC14 — "existing CSV tests still pass unchanged").

### 6. Manual / cross-platform verification (AC13)

Per `AGENTS.md`'s UI-change rule: start the dev server
(`yarn start`), open a budget (use "View demo" for realistic sample data),
and manually export a PDF — check the title, columns, bold group/total rows,
page break + repeated header behavior on a budget with many groups, and a
long category name. Spot check in at least Chrome; note in the PR if
Firefox/Safari/Electron weren't hand-tested in this environment (the repo's
`e2e:desktop` / Electron build can verify the Electron path if time allows).

### 7. Release note

Add `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md` per the convention (e.g.
`add-pdf-budget-export.md`) — use the `writing-release-notes` skill. Mention
the new PDF export option in plain language; no implementation jargon.

### 8. Follow-up issue (font embedding)

Per the Open-Question-1 decision: file a short new GitHub issue (prefixed
🤖 per the repo's bot-comment convention since it's AI-authored) tracking
embedding a Unicode font (e.g. Noto Sans) so ₹ and non-Latin category names
render correctly in the PDF. Link it from the #61 PR description. Do this
only after the main implementation is reviewed and ready, so the follow-up
issue references the real PR number.

## Commit / PR

Follow `.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`:
- Commit messages and PR title prefixed `[AI]`.
- PR title: `[AI] PDF export: add PDF option to Export menu, polish layout (issue #61)` (adjust wording to match final scope).
- Do not fill in the PR template — leave it blank for the human to complete.
- PR body references: `Fixes #61, Relates to #57, #60`.

1	import { send } from '@actual-app/core/platform/client/connection';
2	import { integerToAmount } from '@actual-app/core/shared/util';
3	import type { CategoryGroupEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
4	import { t } from 'i18next';
5	
6	import { stringifyCsv } from '#util/csv';
7	
8	import { collectBudgetMonthRows } from './budgetMonthRows';
9	
10	type BudgetMonthCells = Map<string, unknown>;
11	
12	type BuildBudgetMonthCsvOptions = {
13	  month: string;
14	  categoryGroups: CategoryGroupEntity[];
15	  cells: BudgetMonthCells;
16	  showHiddenCategories: boolean;
17	  decimalPlaces: number;
18	};
19	
20	type CsvRow = [string, string, number | '', number | '', number | ''];
21	
22	// Builds a CSV of one envelope budget month, mirroring the rows and values
23	// shown on the budget page. Subtotals and totals come from the spreadsheet's
24	// own group/total cells so they always match what the page displays.
25	export function buildBudgetMonthCsv({
26	  month,
27	  categoryGroups,
28	  cells,
29	  showHiddenCategories,
30	  decimalPlaces,
31	}: BuildBudgetMonthCsvOptions): string {
32	  function amount(value: number | null): number | '' {
33	    return value == null ? '' : integerToAmount(value, decimalPlaces);
34	  }
35	
36	  const rawRows = collectBudgetMonthRows({
37	    month,
38	    categoryGroups,
39	    cells,
40	    showHiddenCategories,
41	  });
42	
43	  const rows: CsvRow[] = rawRows.map(row => [
44	    row.groupName,
45	    row.categoryName,
46	    amount(row.budgeted),
47	    amount(row.spent),
48	    amount(row.balance),
49	  ]);
50	
51	  return stringifyCsv(rows, [
52	    t('Category Group'),
53	    t('Category'),
54	    t('Budgeted'),
55	    t('Spent'),
56	    t('Balance'),
57	  ]);
58	}
59	
60	export function getBudgetMonthCsvFilename(
61	  budgetName: string | undefined,
62	  month: string,
63	): string {
64	  const safeName = (budgetName ?? '').replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, '').trim();
65	  return `${safeName || 'budget'}-${month}.csv`;
66	}
67	
68	export async function fetchBudgetMonthCells(
69	  month: string,
70	): Promise<BudgetMonthCells> {
71	  const values = await send('envelope-budget-month', { month });
72	  return new Map(values.map(({ name, value }) => [name, value]));
73	}

1	import type { CategoryGroupEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
2	
3	import { collectBudgetMonthRows } from './budgetMonthRows';
4	import type { RawBudgetMonthRowKind } from './budgetMonthRows';
5	
6	// The envelope budget page renders a category group's name and its
7	// Budgeted/Spent/Balance as one combined, bold row (see
8	// `CategoryGroupMonth` in EnvelopeBudgetComponents.tsx) — there is no
9	// separate header-then-subtotal split to preserve. `groupHeader` is used for
10	// that combined row; `groupSubtotal` is kept in the type for the renderer's
11	// vocabulary (per the issue's acceptance criteria) but is never emitted here.
12	export type PdfRowType =
13	  | 'groupHeader'
14	  | 'category'
15	  | 'groupSubtotal'
16	  | 'grandTotal';
17	
18	export type PdfRow = {
19	  type: PdfRowType;
20	  categoryGroup: string;
21	  category: string;
22	  // Already formatted for display; '' for a blank cell.
23	  budgeted: string;
24	  spent: string;
25	  balance: string;
26	};
27	
28	const ROW_TYPE_BY_KIND: Record<RawBudgetMonthRowKind, PdfRowType> = {
29	  group: 'groupHeader',
30	  category: 'category',
31	  income: 'groupHeader',
32	  incomeCategory: 'category',
33	  total: 'grandTotal',
34	  toBudget: 'grandTotal',
35	};
36	
37	type BuildBudgetMonthPdfRowsOptions = {
38	  month: string;
39	  categoryGroups: CategoryGroupEntity[];
40	  cells: Map<string, unknown>;
41	  showHiddenCategories: boolean;
42	  // Formats a raw integer-cent amount using the user's configured currency
43	  // and number format, e.g. a `useFormat()`-bound closure for the
44	  // 'financial' type.
45	  formatAmount: (value: number) => string;
46	};
47	
48	// Turns one envelope budget month into an ordered list of PDF table rows,
49	// reusing the same row traversal the CSV export uses so the two formats
50	// show identical numbers. Each row is tagged with the kind of row it is so
51	// a renderer can style group/total rows distinctly from category rows.
52	export function buildBudgetMonthPdfRows({
53	  month,
54	  categoryGroups,
55	  cells,
56	  showHiddenCategories,
57	  formatAmount,
58	}: BuildBudgetMonthPdfRowsOptions): PdfRow[] {
59	  function amount(value: number | null): string {
60	    return value == null ? '' : formatAmount(value);
61	  }
62	
63	  return collectBudgetMonthRows({
64	    month,
65	    categoryGroups,
66	    cells,
67	    showHiddenCategories,
68	  }).map(row => ({
69	    type: ROW_TYPE_BY_KIND[row.kind],
70	    categoryGroup: row.groupName,
71	    category: row.categoryName,
72	    budgeted: amount(row.budgeted),
73	    spent: amount(row.spent),
74	    balance: amount(row.balance),
75	  }));
76	}
77

import { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo } from 'react';

import { evalArithmetic } from '@actual-app/core/shared/arithmetic';
import { getCurrency } from '@actual-app/core/shared/currencies';
import type { Currency } from '@actual-app/core/shared/currencies';
import {
  amountToInteger,
  currencyToAmount,
  getNumberFormat,
  integerToAmount,
  integerToCurrency,
  parseNumberFormat,
  setNumberFormat,
} from '@actual-app/core/shared/util';
import type { Amount, IntegerAmount } from '@actual-app/core/shared/util';

import { useSyncedPref } from './useSyncedPref';

export type FormatType =
  | 'string'
  | 'number'
  | 'percentage'
  | 'financial'
  | 'financial-with-sign'
  | 'financial-no-decimals';

export type ForEditOptions = {
  /**
   * Format with the currency's full precision even when the `hideFraction`
   * pref is on. Used where the formatted string is parsed back into an
   * `IntegerAmount` later, so dropping the fraction would lose data.
   */
  keepFraction?: boolean;
};

export type UseFormatResult = {
  (value: unknown, type?: FormatType): string;
  forEdit: (value: IntegerAmount, options?: ForEditOptions) => string;
  fromEdit: (
    value: string,
    defaultValue?: number | null,
  ) => IntegerAmount | null;
  /** Scales an `IntegerAmount` down to a decimal `Amount` for the active currency. */
  toAmount: (value: IntegerAmount) => Amount;
  /** Scales a decimal `Amount` up to an `IntegerAmount` for the active currency. */
  fromAmount: (value: Amount) => IntegerAmount;
  currency: Currency;
  /** Whether the `hideFraction` pref is on, so callers don't re-read it. */
  hideFraction: boolean;
};

export type FormatResult = {
  numericValue?: number;
  formattedString: string;
};

function format(
  value: unknown,
  type: FormatType,
  formatter: { format: (value: number) => string },
  decimalPlaces: number,
): FormatResult {
  switch (type) {
    case 'string': {
      const val = JSON.stringify(value);

      if (val.charAt(0) === '"' && val.charAt(val.length - 1) === '"') {
        return { formattedString: val.slice(1, -1) };
      }
      return { formattedString: val };
    }
    case 'number':
      if (typeof value !== 'number') {
        throw new Error(
          'Value is not a number (' + typeof value + '): ' + value,
        );
      }
      return { numericValue: value, formattedString: formatter.format(value) };
    case 'percentage':
      return { formattedString: value + '%' };

```typescript
import { t } from 'i18next';
import type { Styles, UserOptions } from 'jspdf-autotable';

import type { PdfRow } from './budgetMonthPdfRows';

const EMPHASIZED_ROW_STYLES: Partial<Styles> = {
  fontStyle: 'bold',
  fillColor: [235, 235, 235],
};

type AutoTableCellDef = { content: string; styles?: Partial<Styles> };
type AutoTableRow = Record<
  'categoryGroup' | 'category' | 'budgeted' | 'spent' | 'balance',
  AutoTableCellDef
>;

// `groupHeader`/`groupSubtotal`/`grandTotal` all share one emphasized style;
// only `category` rows are left unstyled. `groupSubtotal` is never actually
// emitted by buildBudgetMonthPdfRows (see that file's comment), but is
// handled here anyway since the type allows it.
export function toAutoTableRows(rows: PdfRow[]): AutoTableRow[] {
  return rows.map(row => {
    const styles = row.type === 'category' ? undefined : EMPHASIZED_ROW_STYLES;
    const cell = (content: string): AutoTableCellDef =>
      styles ? { content, styles } : { content };

    return {
      categoryGroup: cell(row.categoryGroup),
      category: cell(row.category),
      budgeted: cell(row.budgeted),
      spent: cell(row.spent),
      balance: cell(row.balance),
    };
  });
}

type BuildBudgetMonthPdfBytesOptions = {
  title: string;
  rows: PdfRow[];
};

// Renders an envelope budget month's already-built PdfRows into a PDF,
// lazy-loading jsPDF/jspdf-autotable so neither appears in the main bundle.
// Does not walk categories or read spreadsheet cells itself — all of that
// data work is done by buildBudgetMonthPdfRows, so the PDF can never show
// different numbers than the CSV export.
export async function buildBudgetMonthPdfBytes({
  title,
  rows,
}: BuildBudgetMonthPdfBytesOptions): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const [{ jsPDF }, { default: autoTable }] = await Promise.all([
    import('jspdf'),
    import('jspdf-autotable'),
  ]);

  const doc = new jsPDF({ orientation: 'portrait', unit: 'pt' });

  doc.setFontSize(14);
  doc.text(title, 40, 40);

  const columns: UserOptions['columns'] = [
    { header: t('Category Group'), dataKey: 'categoryGroup' },
    { header: t('Category'), dataKey: 'category' },
    { header: t('Budgeted'), dataKey: 'budgeted' },
    { header: t('Spent'), dataKey: 'spent' },
    { header: t('Balance'), dataKey: 'balance' },
  ];

  autoTable(doc, {
    startY: 60,
    // Repeats the header row on every page and keeps a row from splitting
    // across a page break.
    showHead: 'everyPage',
    rowPageBreak: 'avoid',
    theme: 'plain',
    styles: { overflow: 'linebreak', cellWidth: 'auto' },
    columnStyles: {
      budgeted: { halign: 'right' },
      spent: { halign: 'right' },
      balance: { halign: 'right' },
    },
    columns,
    body: toAutoTableRows(rows),
    didDrawPage: data => {
      const pageSize = doc.internal.pageSize;
      doc.setFontSize(9);
      doc.text(
        t('Page {{page}}', { page: data.pageNumber }),
        pageSize.getWidth() - 60,
        pageSize.getHeight() - 20,
      );
    },
  });

  return new Uint8Array(doc.output('arraybuffer'));
}

```typescript
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import type { PdfRow } from './budgetMonthPdfRows';
import { toAutoTableRows } from './budgetMonthPdf';

function row(overrides: Partial<PdfRow> = {}): PdfRow {
  return {
    type: 'category',
    categoryGroup: 'Bills',
    category: 'Rent',
    budgeted: '$120.00',
    spent: '-$120.00',
    balance: '$0.00',
    ...overrides,
  };
}

describe('toAutoTableRows', () => {
  it('maps every PdfRow field to a same-named cell', () => {
    const [result] = toAutoTableRows([row()]);

    expect(result.categoryGroup.content).toBe('Bills');
    expect(result.category.content).toBe('Rent');
    expect(result.budgeted.content).toBe('$120.00');
    expect(result.spent.content).toBe('-$120.00');
    expect(result.balance.content).toBe('$0.00');
  });

  it('leaves category rows unstyled', () => {
    const [result] = toAutoTableRows([row({ type: 'category' })]);

    expect(result.category.styles).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it.each(['groupHeader', 'groupSubtotal', 'grandTotal'] as const)(
    'bolds and shades %s rows',
    type => {
      const [result] = toAutoTableRows([row({ type })]);

      expect(result.categoryGroup.styles).toEqual({
        fontStyle: 'bold',
        fillColor: [235, 235, 235],
      });
    },
  );

  it('preserves row order', () => {
    const rows = toAutoTableRows([
      row({ type: 'groupHeader', category: '' }),
      row({ type: 'category', category: 'Rent' }),
      row({ type: 'category', category: 'Power' }),
      row({ type: 'grandTotal', categoryGroup: 'Total', category: '' }),
    ]);

    expect(rows.map(r => r.category.content)).toEqual([
      '',
      'Rent',
      'Power',
      '',
    ]);
  });
});

```

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { buildExportMenuItems } from './BudgetExportMenu';

const labels = {
  exportAsCsv: 'Export as CSV',
  exportAsPdf: 'Export as PDF',
  csvSection: 'CSV',
  pdfSection: 'PDF',
};

const formatMonth = (month: string) => `Formatted ${month}`;

describe('buildExportMenuItems', () => {
  it('offers a plain CSV and PDF entry for a single month', () => {
    expect(buildExportMenuItems(['2026-01'], labels, formatMonth)).toEqual([
      { name: 'csv:2026-01', text: 'Export as CSV' },
      { name: 'pdf:2026-01', text: 'Export as PDF' },
    ]);
  });

  it('groups by format with a labeled section per format for multiple months', () => {
    const items = buildExportMenuItems(
      ['2026-01', '2026-02'],
      labels,
      formatMonth,
    );

    expect(items).toEqual([
      { type: expect.anything(), name: 'CSV', text: '' },
      { name: 'csv:2026-01', text: 'Formatted 2026-01' },
      { name: 'csv:2026-02', text: 'Formatted 2026-02' },
      { type: expect.anything(), name: 'PDF', text: '' },
      { name: 'pdf:2026-01', text: 'Formatted 2026-01' },
      { name: 'pdf:2026-02', text: 'Formatted 2026-02' },
    ]);
  });

  it('lists every visible month under both the CSV and PDF sections', () => {
    const items = buildExportMenuItems(
      ['2026-01', '2026-02', '2026-03'],
      labels,
      formatMonth,
    );

    const csvEntries = items.filter(item => item.name.startsWith('csv:'));
    const pdfEntries = items.filter(item => item.name.startsWith('pdf:'));
    expect(csvEntries).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(pdfEntries).toHaveLength(3);
  });
});

```

```text
1	# Example: Browser-driven web app
2	
3	You have a dev server that serves HTML to a browser. An agent in a
4	headless container can't open a browser window - so "run the app" means
5	launching the dev server, driving a headless Chromium against it, and
6	producing a screenshot that proves the page rendered.
7	
8	Don't write a browser driver. Use `chromium-cli`.
9	
10	## Dev server
11	
12	Find the dev command (`package.json` `scripts.dev`, `Makefile`,
13	README), start it in the background, and wait for it to actually serve:
14	
15	```bash
16	npm run dev &   # or yarn dev, pnpm dev, make serve, ./dev.sh
17	timeout 30 bash -c 'until curl -sf http://localhost:3000 >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done'
18	```
19	
20	Don't `sleep 5` - poll the port. Stop by killing the port's listener
21	-- `lsof -ti:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs -r kill` - before relaunching,
22	or the next run hits `EADDRINUSE`. (`$!` after `npm run dev &` is only
23	the npm wrapper; npm doesn't forward SIGTERM to the server it spawned,
24	so the port kill is what actually frees it.) Avoid `pkill -f` with a
25	broad pattern - it can match the agent's own command line and kill the
26	session.
27	
28	## Drive
29	
30	`chromium-cli` is a headless-Chromium REPL. Pipe a script to stdin:
31	
32	```bash
33	chromium-cli --session app <<'EOF'
34	nav http://localhost:3000
35	wait-for text=Dashboard
36	screenshot
37	click button:has-text("New item")
38	fill input[name="title"] Smoke test
39	press Enter
40	wait-for text=Smoke test
41	screenshot
42	console --errors
43	EOF
44	```
45	
46	Screenshots land in `chromium_cli/sessions/app/screenshots/` (latest
47	symlinked as `screenshot.png`). That's the whole loop: `nav` ->
48	`wait-for` the element you need -> act (`click` / `fill` / `type` /
49	`press`) -> `screenshot` -> `console --errors` to check nothing threw.
50	Full command reference: `chromium-cli` skill, or `help` at the prompt.
51	
52	For iterative debugging, run it under tmux and `send-keys` one command
53	at a time - same commands, same session.
54	
55	**If `chromium-cli` isn't available:** adapt
56	[electron.md](electron.md)'s REPL driver - the structure and commands
57	transfer, but it's `_electron`-specific:
58	import `{ chromium }` instead, launch with
59	`chromium.launch({ args: ['--no-sandbox'] })`, acquire the page via
60	`(await app.newContext()).newPage()` then `goto()` your dev URL, and
61	drop the Electron-only window introspection
62	(`.windows()`/`.firstWindow()`/the `windows` command).
63	
64	## What to put in the skill
65	
66	The project-specific bits only. `chromium-cli` handles the mechanics.
67	
68	- **Dev command + port + stop.** The exact start line, any env vars it
69	  needs, and the `kill` to stop it.
70	- **Auth.** Whatever gets a logged-in session - a `set-cookie` line, a
71	  `fill`/`click` login sequence, or a helper script that does the API
72	  dance and emits the cookie.
73	- **One representative interaction.** Not the whole app - one path that
74	  proves it's running, ending in a screenshot.
75	- **App-specific gotchas.** Only the ones you actually hit.
76	
77	## Gotchas that recur
78	
79	- **React controlled inputs.** `eval el.value = '...'` doesn't fire
80	  React's onChange. Use `fill` / `type` - they go through Playwright's
81	  input pipeline.
82	- **Websockets / long-poll.** `wait-idle` never settles. `wait-for` the
83	  element you actually need.
84	- **Slow first paint.** Vite/Next compile routes on demand; the first
85	  `nav` can take 10s+. `wait-for` handles it; raw `sleep` doesn't.
86	- **`screenshot-element <sel>`** crops to one element - use it when the
87	  diff is in a specific component, not the whole page.
88	- **Check `console --errors` before declaring success.** A page can
89	  render its shell while every data fetch 500s.
90

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.
